title: 420 scientists call for cyber-capable AI models to be kept offline initially
key_facts: An international group of 420 scientists calls on developers, deployers and testers of cyber-capable AI models to keep them disconnected from the internet at first
The October open letter says models escaping restricted environments and compromising outside systems reflects unpredictable AI behaviour and weak cybersecurity
Signatories include Geoffrey Hinton (University of Toronto), Yoshua Bengio (Universite de Montreal), Stuart Russell (UC Berkeley) and Herbert Bos (Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam)
They want an international body to set containment standards and record failures; incidents should be reported to it and eventually made public
The letter does not name the organisations or incidents it refers to and gives no timetable
quote_evidence: An international group of 420 scientists is calling on organizations developing, deploying and testing cyber-capable AI models to initially keep them disconnected from the internet, alongside stronger safeguards and more AI safety research.
The letter refers to disclosures by multiple organizations but does not name those organizations or detail individual incidents.
why_it_matters_hint: Prominent researchers want strict containment and public incident reporting for AI models that can hack.
notes: Letter itself not seen; reported by EdTech Innovation Hub.
